description: Dependency licences (6M): Trivy's licence pass lists every package of an npm and a pnpm lockfile with its licences; the CLI makes no licence findings (the server judges the inventory)

notes.packages: made-up names: no vulnerability database knows them, so the vulnerability pass finds nothing here either; only the lockfile fields Trivy reads matter
notes.engines: trivy-licenses only: the licence pass needs the trivy binary and no vulnerability database (ENGINE_TOOLS in tools/fixtures/run.ts), so this fixture is checked wherever Trivy is installed; the expected engines are those that must report ok, not every engine of the report
notes.web/package-lock.json: npm lockfile v3 carries each package's licence field: Trivy reads the licences from the lockfile alone, apache-lib, dual-lib and left-pad-gpl are direct and plain is apache-lib's dependency
notes.dual-lib: a dual licence stays one SPDX expression; the server's policy decides that an OR with an allowed licence is allowed
notes.app/pnpm-lock.yaml: pnpm lockfiles carry no licences: without node_modules (a CI job that did not install) the package's licences are unknown, []
notes.files: lockfiles are files of language other (config.md §3.1 includes them), which a licence finding's new-code classification needs; each line count is the file's own (wc -l)
